subject: PrivGPU runrate scenarios & scheduler for burst headroom
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@edgeai.co>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Gabe Liu <gabe.liu@acmeai.com>
Date: 2028-07-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: PrivGPU runrate scenarios + scheduler integration

Hey Vanessa,

Quick thank-you for the demo yesterday — the throughput numbers looked promising. We're starting the next stage of our private deployment planning and need to converge on a steady-state runrate target and how Redwood's scheduler/fallbacks will handle multi-minute sustained bursts. Two concrete asks:

1) A recommended runrate envelope (qps/token cadence) you expect a 4x/10x/25x burst to look like for a 1000-GPU private pool.
2) A scheduler integration checklist so our infra team can wire admission control, headroom signals, and egress throttles to the Redwood agent.

I've attached a CSV with our traffic slices (80th/95th/99th windows) and a short doc with our network constraints. Can you loop in the folks who'd be doing the sizing? We're targeting an internal readiness review next Wednesday (2028-07-16).

Thanks,
Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Platform, EdgeAI
Attachments: runrate_sim_inputs.csv (csv stub)

Date: 2028-07-09T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivGPU runrate scenarios + scheduler integration

Hi Samira — thanks for the file. Looping in Karthik and Jonas who will lead the sizing and scheduler work; Laura for rollout coordination.

Quick plan:
- Karthik/Jonas will run 3 scenario sims (baseline, sustained-4x, fat-tail-25x) using your CSV inputs and our KV-cache warming models. Expect a runbook draft by EOD 7/11.
- We'll propose admission-control thresholds and two fallback modes: (A) degrade to a smaller context-length model (soft degrade) and (B) redirect low-priority requests to a burst tier with explicit rate limits.
- Scheduler checklist: signal definitions (headroom_pct, kv_cache_hit, avg_latency_p50/p95), required telemetry hooks, and DocuSign for a short SLO exception if you want hard guarantees during initial ramp.

Can you confirm whether we should include a cold-start warmup window in the sim or assume KV caches are already warmed? That assumption changes the headroom required.

-Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Samira Khan <samira.k@edgeai.co>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-09T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivGPU runrate scenarios + scheduler integration

Vanessa / Samira — I pulled Samira's CSV and ran an initial fast-pass. Attaching a small input slice and the scheduler proposal PDF (high level) for transparency. Notes from the spot check: 

1) Assumption to confirm: cache-warmed vs cold-start. If caches are warm we'll budget ~12-15% idle headroom per pool to absorb transient 4x bursts while honoring p95 latency SLO. If cold-starts happen often, that expands to 35-45% and we should model staged warmup.

2) Network egress: EdgeAI's provided egress cap (3.2 Gbps/node) means we hit network bottlenecks before GPU saturation on some fat-tail scenarios. Proposed mitigation: per-pod egress policer + token-aware batching so we don't saturate individual NICs.

3) Scheduler knobs (proposal highlights):
- admission_window_ms: 1200 (default), tunable down to 600 for priority routes
- headroom_pct: 15 (baseline warmed), 40 (cold)
- burst_tier_rate: 0.6 of steady-state for best-effort requests
- kv_warmup_batch: target warmup qps to reach 80% hit in N minutes

4) Run-rate outputs (very preliminary) for a 1000-GPU private farm (mixed A100-like class):
- baseline steady qps: ~90k requests/min (mixed payloads)
- sustained 4x: ~360k req/min for up to 10 minutes with 15% headroom (warm)
- fat-tail 25x: ~2.25M req/min unacceptable unless you reserve burst capacity or accept p95 latency regressions and fallback.

Next steps: Jonas will run the full sim matrix (network + cache + admission) and return a CSV of scenario outcomes. Samira — please confirm warm vs cold cache and whether you'd accept model-level soft-degrades for best-effort traffic.

Attachments: scheduler_proposal_v1.pdf (pdf stub), sim_input_slice.csv (csv stub)

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. PM, Performance & Capacity
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.k@edgeai.co>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-09T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivGPU runrate scenarios + scheduler integration

All — quick simulation update (summary) ahead of the runbook draft: 

Simulation matrix run (8 scenarios): baseline, 2x, 4x, 8x; each with warm/cold cache and with/without per-pod egress shaping. Key findings: 

- With warm caches and per-pod egress shaping, a 4x sustained for up to 12 minutes keeps p95 within 1.3x of steady-state if headroom_pct=15 and admission_window_ms=1200.
- Cold-cache scenarios drive a tail: headroom_pct must be >=40 or we must pre-warm in stages.
- Egress shaping buys linear improvements for fat-tail loads: without egress shaping, NIC saturation forces token batching to spike, causing p95 to double at ~6x.
- Fallback effectiveness: soft-degrade (shorter context model) recovers 60-80% of throughput with a modest quality loss; redirect-to-burst-tier recovers 30-50% but keeps latency more predictable.

Proposed ops checklist for EdgeAI handoff: 
1) Wire telemetry: headroom_pct, kv_hit_rate, per-pod_egress_bps, p95_latency, queue_depth.
2) Add admission control webhooks with two gates: immediate_reject (hard) and degrade_route (soft).
3) Define SLO override: a DocuSign that allows EdgeAI to accept up to 2x p95 increase for two 30-minute windows per month during ramp.
4) Runbook: warmup choreography (N minutes at X qps per pod), failure-mode steps (rollback to smaller model, enable burst-tier), and contact matrix.

I'll push the CSV outputs and the scenario graphs to the Drive link by EOD 7/10. If EdgeAI confirms cache-warm assumption, we can tighten the headroom_pct estimate and draft the DocuSign language.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
